audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may omit the cash reinvestment required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2026 capital expenditures were $298.921 million and FY2027 expenditures are expected to be higher
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our capital expenditures for fiscal year 2027 to increase compared to fiscal year 2026, mainly due to the purchase of a new manufacturing building in California, continued investment in our manufacturing facilities at our Pathum Thani campus, and ongoing investments in equipment to support the expansion of our manufacturing capacity.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved modeling possibility, not a demonstrated omission: the scenarios grow owner earnings by 8%-10% without an explicit reinvestment schedule, while the filing identifies substantial capacity spending and working-capital expansion. The potential charge is reasonably capable of materially reducing the $7.028-$7.837 billion operating values because FY2026 capital expenditures alone equaled 78.7% of the $380 million OE anchor, although the record does not establish how much was expansionary or already reflected in OE.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance from growth capital expenditure, forecast incremental receivables and inventory net of payables for each growth case, and rerun OE after deducting all scenario-required reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat working-capital liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $875.055 million, or $23.96 per diluted share; 11.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: The cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments are held for working capital purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire filed cash and short-term-investment balance even though the filing says those funds are held for working-capital purposes. The record does not establish how much is indispensable, but the full exposure is $875.055 million—16.1% of bear, 11.0% of base and 10.0% of bull equity value—so even a substantial partial reclassification could materially change the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating liquidity from cash-conversion-cycle requirements, purchase commitments and stress needs; reconcile it with working capital already charged in OE, then add only distributable excess cash and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The historical trend crosses a structural tax-regime change
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2026 Pillar Two expense was $57.447 million, equal to 15.1% of the $380 million OE anchor
audit_findings.evidence: Similar preferential tax treatment was available to us through June 2026 with respect to products manufactured at our Chonburi campus and through June 2020 with respect to products manufactured at our Pinehurst campus.
audit_findings.explanation: The regime mismatch is demonstrated: the trend includes years benefiting from exemptions that have expired, while the principal Chonburi exemption ended in June 2026. FY2026 already includes the $57.447 million Pillar Two charge, so that amount is not itself an omission, but earlier trend years were not normalized and prospective taxes after the exemption expiry remain unresolved. Because the anchor drives every forecast year and terminal value, the prospective tax adjustment is reasonably capable of materially lowering value.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate each historical OE year under the prospective tax regime, allocate income among taxable and incentivized facilities, apply the Building 9 and Navanakorn caps and timing, and rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: An unreserved litigation claim could rank ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: RMB 400 million claimed principal plus unquantified interest from March 1, 2000
audit_findings.evidence: The Plaintiffs requested that the Court order FEHC to return the unjust enrichment to the Plaintiffs in the amount of RMB 400 million, with interest from March 1, 2000, and order Jian and Casix to bear joint and several liability for all payment obligations of FEHC.
audit_findings.explanation: The lawsuit and claimed amount are demonstrated, but a liability is not: two lower courts dismissed on jurisdictional grounds, retrial acceptance was not a merits ruling, and the company states that exposure cannot yet be quantified. An adverse joint-and-several judgment could reduce equity value, potentially substantially after decades of interest, but the record supplies neither probability nor enforceable exposure and therefore cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain counsel's merits probability, enforceability analysis and principal-plus-interest exposure range; include a probability-weighted bridge deduction or explicit adverse litigation scenario.

audit_findings.title: Post-year-end borrowing creates an interest cost absent from the historical numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $75.0 million loan principal and $76.9 million facility acquisition filed; interest cost and net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Under the 2019 Credit Facility Agreement, on August 17, 2026, the Borrower and the Bank entered into a term loan agreement (the “Term Loan Agreement”) in the original principal amount of Thai baht 2.50 billion (approximately $ 75.0 million based on the applicable exchange rate as of August 17, 2026).
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated: the September 5 valuation uses the June 26 balance sheet and historical OE even though the facility acquisition and term borrowing occurred before the valuation date. The acquisition uses cash that the bridge treats as available, the loan proceeds were designated for capital expenditures rather than distribution, and future equity-level OE must bear interest. The record omits the loan rate, repayment schedule and valuation-date cash deployment, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a valuation-date cash-and-debt roll-forward covering the acquisition, loan proceeds and subsequent capital spending; obtain the loan rate and amortization schedule, exclude operating-use cash from the bridge, and rerun OE with interest and related tax effects.

audit_findings.title: The bridge omits an unfunded employee severance claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.095 million, or $0.93 per diluted share; 0.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: There are no separate plan assets held in respect to these liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation is demonstrated, but a separate deduction may double count amounts already captured through service expense and forecast settlements. Even assuming the entire gross liability is omitted and deducted without tax adjustment, it reduces bear value by only 0.6%, base value by 0.4% and bull value by 0.4%, which is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether projected OE includes payments against the opening obligation; if not, deduct only the settlement amount not already reflected in forecast cash flows.
